steps.say: Meet the McKinley assistant, a prototype that helps residents and future residents get answers at any hour.
It runs on made-up data, and it tells people up front that they're talking to an A.I.
steps.caption: It runs on made-up data, and it tells people up front that they're talking to an AI.

steps.say: First, someone looking for an apartment taps: I need a place soon.
The assistant asks only what it needs. Which community?
Which days?
And what time of day?
Then it shows a summary to check. Nothing is sent until they say so.
One tap, and the tour request is saved for the leasing team.
Now let's sign in as Marisol, a resident at Heron Lake Apartments.
Her air conditioning has stopped cooling again, and she's upset.
The assistant can see her earlier repair visits, so it doesn't make her troubleshoot again. It flags a repeat issue for a manager.
It asks one question: may maintenance come in if she's not home?
Everything else comes from her account, and each line shows where it came from.
She sends it, and gets a reference number right away.
She can check on all her requests at any time.
Safety comes first.
When Theo writes that he smells gas, the assistant skips everything else.
It tells him to get outside and call nine one one, and puts an urgent note at the top of the staff queue.
steps.caption: It tells him to get outside and call 911, and puts an urgent note at the top of the staff queue.

steps.say: Residents can also write in Spanish.
Valeria gets the same careful help, in her own language.
And it protects residents' information.
When someone claiming to be a contractor asks for a gate code, it politely declines and passes a note to the office instead.
Behind the scenes, staff have their own console.
Saved requests lists everything the assistant prepared, with urgent items first.
The conversation inspector shows each step: what the person wrote, what the assistant decided, and why.
The McKinley assistant: quicker answers for residents, clearer handoffs for staff, and safety first.
Next, we would connect it to McKinley's real systems and keep testing its safety rules. Thanks for watching.
